adopted: Keep race-relative, 4th-corner-position-adjusted ACI as an internal closing-performance signal.
Keep prev3_aci_median as the primary ACI ability/repetition baseline; do not replace it with same-demand median.
Use course/surface/distance demand type only to interpret what kind of performance is required: sharp_closing, balanced, or sustained_position.

sustained_position never means that a slower last-3F time is inherently better; it means sharp last-3F receives less weight while position, sustained speed and deceleration resistance receive relatively more weight.
Use reproducibility as a confidence/current-value modifier. Large objective volatility lowers reproducibility confidence but does not erase peak ability.
Treat psychological labels such as mood as unsupported unless objective pre-race evidence exists; performance volatility is the modelled observable.
Prediction-time pace S/M/M-H/H and current track condition override historical course averages when they conflict.
rejected: Do not mechanically replace prev3_aci_median with same-demand ACI median: next-start validation deteriorated.
Do not rank horses with confidence_adjusted_aci_v11 or subtract a numerical volatility penalty directly from peak ability: next-start validation deteriorated.
Do not create a public 10th evaluation axis for ACI.
Do not double-count the same closing-performance evidence in pace, ability and Time Index.
